reasoning: The two clear sites are where the finding says (sort_kokkos :2726-2738 and setup_pre_neighbor :319-331, both gated on '!setupflag'), and their justifying comments (:2719-2725, :302-317) both assert 'nothing had pushed the host arrays create_bodies() wrote to the device, so the device copies hold uninitialized data'. That premise is false, and I traced every step of why. (a) The KK constructor itself calls grow_arrays(atom->nmax) (:77), i.e. FixRigidSmallKokkos::grow_arrays, which takes the !tied_initialized branch, copies create_bodies()' data out of the base memory->grow arrays into the new tied DualViews and ends with k_bodyown/k_atom2body/k_bodytag/k_xcmimage/k_displace.modify_host() (:1728-1732). So the views enter setup HOST-MODIFIED with real data. (b) pre_exchange() begins 'if (!setupflag) return;' (:226), so nothing clears that claim before the setup exchange. (c) The constructor sets exchange_comm_device = 1 and sort_device = 1 for the device instantiation (:92-95), and CommKokkos::exchange() (src/KOKKOS/comm_kokkos.cpp:1003-1035) therefore takes 'exchange_device<LMPDeviceType>()' and calls the fix's pack_exchange_kokkos. (d) pack_exchange_kokkos opens with 'k_bodytag.template sync<DeviceType>(); k_xcmimage...; k_displace...; k_vatom...; k_atom2body...; k_bodyown.template sync<DeviceType>();' (:1820-1825) -- that is exactly the push the comment says never happened -- and the pack/copylist scan plus unpack_exchange_kokkos then migrate the data on the device and mark the views device-modified (:1987-1998). So on the first run the device claim is REAL and the host mirrors are the pre-exchange copy; clearing it and re-declaring the host authoritative (sort_kokkos then does 'k_bodytag.template sync<LMPDeviceType>()' at :2742, pushing the stale host copy back over the migrated one) loses the migration. One point in the code's favour that the finding does not mention, and which I checked: the sort itself is safe -- sort_kokkos syncs the freshly sorted device copies back to the host at :2789-2801 when !setupflag, so the permutation is not lost. The damage is confined to atoms that actually changed owner in the setup-time exchange; for a freshly read data file that is usually none, which is why this has not shown up.
fix: On the first run, retire the device claim by syncing it down rather than discarding it. In sort_kokkos (:2726-2738) replace each 'k_X.clear_sync_state(); k_X.modify_host();' with 'k_X.sync_host(); k_X.modify_host();' and in setup_pre_neighbor (:319-331) replace each 'k_X.clear_sync_state();' with 'k_X.sync_host();'. Also call copy_body_host() alongside, since the same setup-time exchange compacted body[]/nlocal_body on the device while the host body[] was left at its pre-exchange contents. Finally, correct the two comments -- pack_exchange_kokkos's leading sync<DeviceType>() means the device copies are never uninitialized once the constructor's grow_arrays() has run.
